name: Yb2O3 bixbyite 598K
citation: A. Saiki, N. Ishizawa, N. Mizutani and M. Kato. Structural Change of C-Rare Earth Sesquioxides Yb2O3 and Er2O3 as a Function of Temperature. Journal of the Ceramic Association, Japan 93 (1985), 649-654.
recommendation: ordered experimental source candidate; native FEFF validation pending
method: Experimental single-crystal Mo K-alpha four-circle X-ray diffraction with temperature control; full-matrix least-squares refinement. Exact temperature established by matching cell and all variable coordinates to the original table.
synthesis_conditions: Arc-image floating-zone growth of synthetic crystals; original experimental section describes precursor calcination at 1200 degrees Celsius for 24 hours and growth near 2500 degrees Celsius. These are preparation temperatures, not diffraction temperatures.
notes: This is a 598 K structure, not a room-temperature model. COD omitted the temperature tag; the original table supplies the identification.
The parser unique-site order is Yb 24d first and Yb 8b second: weights 0.75 and 0.25 respectively. Do not assume site 1 always has weight 0.25.
Trivalent Yb oxide is not a divalent or mixed-valence Yb reference.

The crystallographic model is an ordered trivalent reference. FEFF L3 EXAFS paths require experimental validation and do not establish 4f multiplet structure, mixed valence, white-line intensity, calibrated S02, or absolute coordination number. No electronic-state or magnetic accuracy is implied by crystallographic agreement.
All variable coordinates and the unit cell are from this exact downloaded source; no element substitution, coordinate replacement, cell rescaling or symmetrization was written to the CIF.
Explicit full occupancies in raw CIF.
